Part 2&3 事件 EVENTS

Describe an occasion when many people were smiling

描述一个很多人都微笑的场合

⚠️ AI 范例，仅供学习 — IELTS 口语全程独立完成，背诵照搬 AI 答案会被考官识别为背稿。

Part 2 话题卡片

Describe an occasion when many people were smiling

  • When it happened (这件事发生在什么时候)
  • Who you were with (你和谁在一起)
  • What happened (发生了什么)
  • And explain why most people were smiling (并解释为什么大多数人都在微笑)

问题与答案

Cue CardDescribe an occasion when many people were smiling

I'd like to describe an occasion when almost everyone around me was smiling, and that was the evening performance at my school's sports event. It happened in my second year of high school, on the last day of the annual sports meeting. The whole school gathered in the big outdoor stadium, and the evening show was the grand finale of the event. I was there with my classmates, and we had all been looking forward to it for weeks, because each class had prepared a performance. The stage was set up in the middle of the field, with colourful lights and loud music, and the atmosphere was electric. I remember our class performed a dance routine, and although we had practised for a month, we were all nervous. When we finished, the whole crowd cheered, and I could see everyone in the audience smiling and clapping. The reason most people were smiling is that the performances were genuinely entertaining, and the whole event had a joyful, competitive spirit. Teachers were smiling too, which was rare, because they were proud of their students. What struck me most was how the smiles spread across the whole stadium, from the performers on stage to the parents in the stands. Looking back, it was one of the happiest evenings of my school life, and I still remember the warmth of that moment whenever I think about it.

高二学校运动会最后一天的晚上表演，全校聚在操场，我们班跳了练一个月的舞蹈，表演很精彩；全场欢呼，老师家长都在微笑，是我校园生活最快乐的夜晚之一。

Q2Do you think people who like to smile are more friendly?

Generally speaking, yes, I think people who smile often come across as more friendly and approachable. A smile is a universal signal of warmth, and it makes others feel comfortable. Having said that, a smile doesn't always mean genuine friendliness, because some people smile out of politeness. So I'd say smiling helps, but real friendliness is shown through actions as well.

爱笑的人通常显得更友好、易接近，微笑是温暖的通用信号；但微笑不一定代表真心友好，有人出于礼貌，真正的友好还要看行动。

Q3Why do most people smile in photographs?

I think most people smile in photographs because a smile is seen as the standard way to look happy and presentable. When we take a photo, we want to record a pleasant moment, and a smile makes the picture look warm and positive. In my country, people often say 'say cheese' to get everyone to smile naturally. Having said that, some people prefer a serious or stylish look in photos, so it really depends on the person and the occasion.

拍照时多数人微笑，因为微笑是显得开心得体的标准方式，让照片温暖积极；我国常说"茄子"让大家自然笑；也有人喜欢酷酷的表情，看人和场合。

Q4Do women smile more than men? Why?

I'd say, in many cultures, women do tend to smile more than men, although it's not a biological rule. One reason is social expectation, because women are often taught to be pleasant and agreeable, while men are expected to appear serious or strong. That said, this is changing, and nowadays more men feel free to smile openly, especially in casual settings.

很多文化里女性确实比男性笑得多，但这不是生理规律；社会期待女性亲切随和、男性严肃坚强；正式照片里女性常大笑而男性微笑或面无表情，不过现在正在改变。

Q5Do people smile more when they are younger or older?

I think people smile more when they are younger, generally speaking. Children smile easily because they experience joy more directly and don't worry about appearances. As people grow older, they face more stress, like work and family responsibilities, which can make them smile less. So I'd say smiling tends to decrease in the middle years, but can return later.

总体说人年轻时笑得多，孩子直接感受快乐不担心形象；成年后面临工作家庭压力笑得更少；但退休老人比中年人笑得多，因为时间多了，微笑在中年减少、晚年回归。

Q6Is smiling important in your culture?

Yes, smiling is quite important in my culture, especially in social and business situations. A smile is seen as a sign of politeness and goodwill, and it helps build relationships. Having said that, in my country, people sometimes smile to hide embarrassment or to avoid conflict, so a smile doesn't always mean happiness. On the whole, though, smiling is definitely valued as a social skill.

微笑在我国文化中很重要，尤其在社交和商务场合，被视为礼貌和善意的标志；初次见面微笑让交流更顺畅；但有时人们用微笑掩饰尴尬或避免冲突，微笑不一定代表开心。

Q7Are there any occasions when people need to pretend to smile?

Yes, there are quite a few occasions when people have to pretend to smile. For example, in customer service, workers are expected to smile even when they're tired or dealing with difficult customers. I think this kind of smile is more about social harmony than genuine emotion. Having said that, pretending to smile too often can be exhausting, which is why some people find service jobs quite draining.

有不少场合需要假笑，如客服人员再累也要对难缠顾客微笑，婚礼、商务晚宴上为礼貌而笑；这种微笑更多为社交和谐而非真实情感，但常假笑很累人。
